content.rationale: the page composition of the viewer: media/webview.html serves the panel regions the page interface names and links the four stylesheets the composed page uses, including styles/search.css, so the search field and its match marks are styled by the module that owns them; src/webview/main.ts is the composition root that receives the graph across the webview seam, builds and orders it, and attaches the renderer, the interaction state, the keyboard equivalents, the presentation, the fit action, the detail panel and find-by-text search to those regions. The search is attached exactly once, after the interaction controller exists, with the canvas, the queued controller, the current graph and its labels. Every later graph is a revision swap: the interaction state keeps the selection, pan and zoom, the detail panel re-renders the selected node, and the search is handed the new graph and labels, so the active query re-marks the reloaded graph and the same field keeps its value instead of a second controller being attached. The standard page lifecycle notifications (pagehide, beforeunload, unload) dispose the search, so no field, listener or match mark outlives the page. The detail panel's four relationship sections list each id in its place as the entry the id is: an id the graph has a node for is listed as an activatable control, and a pointer click or Enter or Space while that entry has the focus runs the same selection a click on the node's own box runs, so the selection moves and the panel re-renders the named node's detail, while an id whose other edge end names no node document stays listed as the plain id and is inert, selecting nothing, leaving the detail as it was and reporting no error. Each listed id is marked, on the element that holds that id and no other, with the recorded vocabulary of two class names (sqwusxql): an id the graph has a node document for carries detail__entry, and an id that names none carries detail__entry--inert as its whole class. Exactly one of the two is on any listed entry — never neither and never both, and never on a container holding more than one id — so the markup is always readable as the answer to which case the entry is, and the class follows the id's own case rather than the section it is listed in. The panel authors no appearance beyond that mark: it declares no style rule, no colour, no cursor and no hover or focus treatment, and the look of a listed id is carried through these two names by the stylesheet rules written against them, as the appearance decisions settle it (mwwxxzyk, tvoouwkn, rqrlnzny, qnmuwwvw, vvzptxmz, mplxzxnm, kpkstnps) and as the composition states it here without restating or narrowing any of those commitments. A second mark sits beside that pair, on a different entry and for a different case: a node whose content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths shows that value in the Content section's monospaced block with the content type on the line above and each path, in the order the list gives them, as an entry of its own — the element that holds that path and nothing else, whose whole class is detail__ref (ppkkmxxu) — so no listed-entry name reaches a path and the markup and the stylesheet meet on that one name, exactly as they meet on the two above. The block keeps the whole value, the type and every path, so the panel and the node's ref list cannot disagree about which files the body lives in, and the entries add no text, no label and no order of their own. The panel declares no appearance for that name either: the entry reads as the visible link squvoxyr commits it to through the rules the stylesheet writes against the name, and the panel fixes only the name those rules select. Each such entry is a control the keyboard can reach, and activating it — a pointer click, or Enter or Space while it has the focus — posts the page's request for that repo-relative path to be opened in the editor as one message of the page's own seam, { type: "openRef", path }, beside the node-open request the double-click already posts (rptlovpt, trxzsqpv). The request names the path and nothing else: the page does not select a node, does not change the detail region and does not move the viewport on a ref path's activation, it resolves no path and opens nothing itself — the host owns how the path is found and opened, as it owns the node document the double-click asks for — and a ref path's activation stays the Content section's own, neither re-triggering the double-click nor reaching the listed ids' activation (kwxutvpw). A value whose ref is inline shows no path and so offers nothing to activate here, and the paths themselves stay what qwzwpxws presents, in the order it presents them. The composition owns only the page shell and the entry point: the renderer, interaction, keyboard, presentation, detail and search modules keep their own behaviour.
